Job Description

Position Overview:

Follett Higher Education is a leading educational service provider and omnichannel retailer, providing students, faculty, staff, parents, and fans with the course materials, learning tools, and retail services needed to successfully support the collegiate journey. Follett Higher Education supports over 6 million students through its 1,100 physical and 1,750 eCommerce campus stores across North America.

This is a high-visibility opportunity to lead a commerce platform transformation on a national scale. The VP of Engineering, Commerce Platform
owns the technical strategy, architecture, and delivery of Follett's ecommerce and point of sale systems, including the ongoing migration from a legacy technology stack to Shopify. This role has final architectural authority over the platform, impacting how millions of students and fans shop and pay for years to come.

The VP brings deep technical credibility, setting direction with conviction, and earning trust across engineering teams. Application Development, QA, and DevOps all report into this role. The VP partners closely with the SVP of Ecommerce, who owns product management and business decisions for ecommerce, while this role owns how those decisions get built, scaled, and operated.

This role owns engineering culture, building a team where engineers own outcomes in partnership with product and leadership, rather than simply executing requirements handed to them.

Responsibilities:

Platform Architecture & Migration

Own end-to-end architecture for ecommerce and POS systems, including the transition from legacy stack to Shopify.
Set technical direction and make final architecture calls across the environment, driving toward the organization's go-forward technology stack.
Act as the subject-matter expert across the modern ecommerce technology stack, including loyalty programs, promotions and pricing engines, and analytics/personalization platforms, to inform architecture decisions that scale across the Follett store network.
Maintain technical standards and architectural integrity across the engineering organization.

Engineering & Delivery Leadership

Lead Application Development, QA, and DevOps teams, setting delivery standards and technical practices across all three functions.
Ensure platform performance, instrumentation, scalability, reliability, and availability to meet the needs of the business and its institutional and student customers.
Drive modern engineering practices appropriate to the team's scale and maturity.
Own technology lifecycle decisions, including system upgrades, platform migrations, and modernization efforts within ecommerce and POS.

Cross-Functional Partnership

Partner closely with the SVP of Ecommerce on roadmap sequencing, tradeoffs, and prioritization, co-owning outcomes while maintaining clear decision rights between technical execution and business/product ownership.
Work across engineering, sales, institutional partners, and operations to balance platform modernization with ongoing academic-calendar-driven operational needs.
Serve as the technical voice in cross-functional planning for ecommerce and POS initiatives.

Engineering Culture & Talent Leadership

Build, mentor, and retain a high-performing engineering organization across App Dev, QA, and DevOps.
Foster a culture of ownership, where teams partner with product and leadership to own outcomes rather than only executing requirements.
Establish clear performance expectations and growth paths for engineering leaders and their teams.
Raise the bar for technical hiring across the organization.

Secure Development & Risk Awareness

Ensure secure development and deployment practices are embedded in engineering workflows, in partnership with the separate security/compliance function that owns security overall.
Maintain working knowledge of data privacy and security considerations relevant to ecommerce and POS systems (e.g., PII handling, data residency) to inform architecture decisions.

Requirements

Bachelor's degree in related field or equivalent
12--15+ years in software engineering, including 5--7+ years in senior engineering leadership (Director, VP, or Head of Engineering) managing multiple teams through leads and managers.
Direct ecommerce software engineering experience, having built or scaled systems for online storefronts, checkout, cart, or order management.
Proven experience leading a legacy-to-modern platform migration.
Expert fluency in modern web technology and architecture patterns.
Experience owning DevOps/CI-CD and QA functions as part of an engineering organization, not app development alone.
Demonstrated track record of building engineering teams with a strong culture of ownership.

Preferred

Shopify experience, whether platform architecture, app development, or merchant-side engineering leadership.
Retail or ecommerce industry background, with collegiate or course materials retail experience being a stronger plus than general retail.
Point-of-sale (POS) systems experience.
Master's degree in technical or business field.

About the Opportunity

The organization is seeking a hands-on, multi-disciplinary Chief Technology Officer to lead its end-to-end technology organization, spanning product engineering, IT infrastructure, and corporate and platform cybersecurity.

Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer and partnering with executive leadership, this executive provides comprehensive oversight across technology, enterprise systems, and risk management. The Chief Product, Engineering, and Data Officer reports directly to this role.

This is a full-time, remote position based in the United States.

Key Responsibilities

Drive overall technology strategy, cloud infrastructure, and technical execution for the organization's core SaaS platform.
Manage the enterprise technology budget and drive cost optimization across software licensing, infrastructure procurement, hardware lifecycles, and vendor contracts.
Partner with executive leadership to transition new products from beta to market launch while actively managing technical debt.
Advise the CEO and Board of Directors on enterprise technical risk, disaster recovery, business continuity planning, and corporate cyber resilience.
Oversee day-to-day corporate IT operations, including endpoint management, automated provisioning and deprovisioning, and multi-tier helpdesk support.
Administer enterprise productivity suites and communication architectures while enforcing zero-trust access controls, single sign-on (SSO), and document retention policies.
Oversee business system infrastructure in close alignment with organizational leadership to ensure high uptime and integration security.
Direct organization-wide information security initiatives across corporate endpoints, networks, and SaaS tools.
Establish and audit enterprise IT policies, including acceptable use, zero-trust identity and access management (IAM), data loss prevention (DLP), and offboarding protocols.
Enforce compliance and audit readiness—including SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, ISO 27001, and c3/c4 non-profit legal boundaries—in collaboration with Legal, HR, and Finance.
Evaluate alpha projects and proofs of concept across departments, guiding execution to integrate them into the core SaaS platform or architect them as standalone, scalable services.
Mitigate vendor lock-in risk by establishing standardized data portability and integration frameworks across corporate SaaS applications.
Serve as direct manager to the Chief Product, Engineering, and Data Officer (CPEDO), establishing shared goals and aligning product, engineering, and data strategies with enterprise infrastructure and security standards.
Partner with the CPEDO on budget, resourcing, and prioritization trade-offs across product, engineering, and data initiatives.
Build, mentor, and scale a service-oriented IT and security team aligned with organizational growth objectives.
Establish pragmatic automated internal processes that maintain rigorous security standards without introducing operational friction for staff.

Qualifications

12+ years of progressive IT leadership experience, including roles such as Director of IT, Head of IT/Operations Technology, VP of IT, or Chief Technology Officer.
Demonstrated experience managing enterprise IT and information security stacks, zero-trust architectures, IAM, and automated endpoint management.
Experience driving capital and operational expenditure (CapEx/OpEx) strategies for corporate IT, including SaaS license management, hardware procurement cycles, and third-party vendor governance.
Proven track record leading enterprise security operations and successfully navigating SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 audit cycles.
Expertise in architecting, securing, and administering enterprise collaboration platforms and workplace productivity suites.
Proven track record of building and leading technical teams across a broad range of expertise.
Experience building or scaling an internal IT function through periods of organizational growth.
Demonstrated ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to non-technical staff, executive leadership, and Board members.

Role details

About Us

We are Sila, a next-generation battery materials company. Our mission is to power the world’s transition to clean energy. To create this future, our team is building a better lithium-ion battery from the inside out today. We engineer and manufacture ground-breaking battery materials that significantly increase the energy density of batteries, while reducing their size and weight. The result? Smaller more powerful batteries that can unlock innovation in consumer devices and accelerate the mass adoption of electric cars to eliminate our dependence on fossil fuels. We're tackling one of the biggest challenges of our time every day, and together we're redefining what's possible.

Are you ready to be a part of a team committed to changing the world?

Who You Are

You’re an engineering leader with the people and technical skills to bring the next generation of lithium-ion batteries to market. You’ll lead a team helping to deploy Sila’s materials in the consumer, industrial and automotive markets through qualification with cell suppliers and OEMs. You will use your experience as a technical individual contributor and as a leader of technical teams to act as a “player-coach” in the deployment of Sila anode material with customers.

You’ll guide collaboration with technical and business teams at Sila as well as external partners and customers and help the team set and reach ambitious, realistic goals by building streamlined systems, setting clear responsibilities, empowering team members, and owning the team’s and Sila’s success.

Facilitate collaboration between groups (such as Product, Business Development, and R&D) at Sila and with external partners through direct communication, information review, and coaching

jobs.description:
Company Description
Portfolio Management Group (PMG) is the student‑managed investment fund at Georgia State University, overseeing more than $1.6M in assets under management. PMG focuses on developing future investment professionals through hands‑on experience in equity research, security analysis, and portfolio construction using real capital. Operating under a long‑only equity mandate benchmarked to the S&P 500, PMG emphasizes disciplined research, collaboration, and long‑term investment thinking. Members receive structured training, mentorship, and practical exposure to evaluating investment opportunities, monitoring portfolio performance, and presenting investment recommendations. The organization’s mission is to equip students with technical, analytical, and professional skills, while building a strong community and network for careers in investment management and finance.
Role Description
The Vice President of Engineering is a full-time remote role responsible for leading the design, development, and maintenance of technology solutions that support PMG’s investment research, portfolio management, and operational workflows. This role oversees engineering teams, sets technical direction, and ensures alignment between product roadmap and organizational goals. Day-to-day responsibilities include managing software development projects, prioritizing and planning engineering initiatives, and partnering with product and investment stakeholders to define requirements and deliver scalable tools. The Vice President of Engineering will establish best practices in coding, testing, deployment, and documentation, and will mentor team members to foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement. The role also involves monitoring system performance, ensuring data integrity and security, and evaluating new technologies that can enhance PMG’s analytical and reporting capabilities.
Qualifications

Demonstrated Engineering Management experience, including setting technical strategy, building processes, and developing high-performing engineering teams.
Strong Team Leadership skills with a track record of mentoring, performance management, and fostering inclusive, collaborative engineering cultures.
Hands-on Software Development expertise in modern languages, frameworks, and tools relevant to data, analytics, or financial applications.
Proficiency in Project Management, including planning, prioritization, risk management, and delivering complex initiatives on time and within scope.
Experience in Product Development, working closely with stakeholders to translate requirements into user-centric, scalable technical solutions.
Background in or familiarity with finance, investment management, or data-intensive domains is highly beneficial.
Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively in a remote environment and across multidisciplinary teams.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field; advanced degree or equivalent practical experience is a plus.
